pathway.title: DYCOM INDUSTRIES INC — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: First, the leverage story is a step-up and a partial reversal. Debt of 2,840.0 million at FY2026 against 950.0 million a year earlier reflects the Power Solutions acquisition, and constructed gross leverage of 2.96x at August 1, 2026 is below the 3.85x at FY2026 only because the LTM earnings base now includes Building Systems and strong Communications growth; the ratios are not pro forma, not covenant ratios and sensitive to the 53-week FY2026 (Documentary Fact inputs, Analyst Interpretation). Second, interest burden is understated by cash interest: LTM cash interest of 86.4 million sits well below the run-rate of about 148.9 million, so the reported cover of 11.10x is a ceiling and about 6.45x the cautious figure. Third, liquidity is large but not unconditional: 1,086.5 million of liquidity, no revolver draw and a maturity wall that starts in April 2029, offset by cash that fell from 709.2 million at FY2026 to 340.1 million at August 1, 2026, a negative six-month free cash flow of 54.2 million and 367.4 million of supplier finance. Fourth, customer concentration and uncommitted volumes make revenue sensitive to a few carriers, with backlog of 12,242 million an indicator rather than a commitment. Fifth, Building Systems is both the growth driver and the newest risk: Q2 2027 revenue of 397.5 million and Non-GAAP Adjusted EBITDA of 97.2 million on fixed-price and modified-fixed-price work, with a preliminary purchase price allocation for National Technology Integrators and goodwill plus intangibles of 2,534.3 million exceeding equity of 2,063.9 million. Sixth, the information that would settle the credit view is missing: the executed credit agreement and indenture, covenant EBITDA and ratios, pro forma acquired EBITDA, ownership and restricted-payment capacity.

runs.text: Strengths. Recurring contract base and backlog: 94.0% of Q2 2027 revenue from multi-year master service agreements and other long-term contracts and backlog of 12,242 million support revenue durability (Documentary Fact). Liquidity and maturity profile: 1,086.5 million of liquidity, 746.4 million of undrawn revolver, and a first major maturity in April 2029 limit refinancing risk (Documentary Fact inputs). Earnings and cash generation: Adjusted EBITDA of 737.7 million in FY2026 against 576.3 million in FY2025 and 959.8 million on LTM Q2 2027, with LTM free cash flow of 485.3 million (Documentary Fact inputs, constructed LTM). Equity used in acquisitions and no dividends: part of the Power Solutions and National Technology Integrators consideration was paid in shares and no cash dividend is paid, which limits cash leakage (Documentary Fact; the behavior reading of Neutral or Mixed is Analyst Interpretation). Higher-margin diversification: Building Systems Adjusted EBITDA of 97.2 million on revenue of 397.5 million in Q2 2027 broadens the earnings base beyond carrier fiber work (Documentary Fact for the figures; durability of the margin is Analyst Interpretation because the contracts are fixed-price and the allocation is preliminary).

Weaknesses. Customer concentration: AT&T, Verizon and Lumen supplied 50.2% of FY2026 revenue combined by customer name, customers may terminate for convenience and are not committed to volumes (Documentary Fact). Leverage step-up and floating-rate exposure: debt of 2,842.7 million at August 1, 2026, about 82% floating-rate at FY2026, no interest-rate hedge disclosed (Documentary Fact; constructed ratios are Analyst Interpretation). Interest cover cushion thinner than headline: about 6.45x on run-rate interest against 11.10x on cash interest (Analyst Interpretation on constructed inputs). Working capital intensity: days sales outstanding of 101, unbilled receivables of 1,334,390 thousand of 2,281,043 thousand gross receivables, and a negative six-month free cash flow of 54.2 million (Documentary Fact). Claims outside the debt figure: supplier finance of 367.4 million, performance and other surety bonds of 1,215.8 million and operating lease liabilities of 228.7 million (Documentary Fact; sensitivity to supplier finance withdrawal is Analyst Interpretation). Asset base is largely intangible: goodwill plus intangible assets of 2,534.3 million exceed total stockholders' equity of 2,063.9 million, so tangible net worth is negative, which is a mechanic for loss absorption rather than a recovery conclusion (Documentary Fact inputs, constructed comparison). Financial policy opacity: new 150.0 million buyback authorization on August 26, 2026 beside rising debt, with restricted-payment capacity, covenant EBITDA and ownership information unavailable (Documentary Fact and Insufficient Information).

runs.text: Power Solutions, LLC (Maryland, electrical infrastructure for data centers and other critical facilities, Greater Washington D.C., Maryland and Virginia area) was acquired under a Unit Purchase Agreement dated November 18, 2025 with Project Eastern Shore, LLC as seller. The preliminary purchase price was 1.95 billion on a cash-free, debt-free basis, payable as a mix of Dycom common stock (1,011,069 shares, 15% of the preliminary price, 292.5 million at signing) and cash, with a purchase price adjustment escrow, a termination right and an outside date of May 18, 2026 (10-Q Q3 FY26 page:25). The deal closed on December 23, 2025: cash of 1,644.9 million (1,628.6 million net of cash acquired), shares valued at 351.0 million at closing and assumed seller debt of 64.8 million, with total consideration of 1,995.9 million in the 10-K (the cash and share amounts together) and 2,008.7 million in the latest 10-Q after a 12.8 million working capital adjustment recorded in Q1 2027; the assumed seller debt is listed separately from total consideration (10-K page:99; 10-Q Q2 FY27 page:35). Status: completed, with the allocation of the purchase price still preliminary in the 10-Q.

Financing: on signing, Dycom obtained a debt commitment letter from Bank of America, N.A., BofA Securities, Inc. and Goldman Sachs Bank USA for a 1,000 million senior secured Term Loan A, a 700 million 364-day bridge facility and a 445 million Term Loan A backstop to refinance existing debt (10-Q Q3 FY26 page:25). The executed structure on December 23, 2025 differed: a 600.0 million 364-day secured bridge, Term Loan A increased from 440.0 million to 1,540.0 million, revolver commitments increased from 650.0 million to 800.0 million and maturities extended to December 23, 2030. On January 27, 2026 a First Amendment established an 800 million senior secured Term Loan B, due January 27, 2033, whose proceeds refinanced the bridge, paid fees and funded cash to the balance sheet (10-K page:112). The 4.50% senior notes due 2029 (500.0 million) were not touched. Effect on liquidity and leverage is in the CP-1 financial base: debt of 2,840.0 million at January 31, 2026 against 950.0 million a year earlier, cash of 709.2 million at January 31, 2026, and revolver availability of 746.4 million. Debt issuance costs of 33,870 thousand were paid and a loss on debt extinguishment of 7,268 thousand was recorded in FY2026 (10-K page:83, page:85).

National Technology Integrators, LLC (Maryland, low-voltage engineering and construction, in Building Systems) was agreed on May 22, 2026 for a stated total of 275.0 million, closed on July 2, 2026 for total consideration of 271.4 million (cash 226.4 million, 225.4 million net of cash acquired, plus 95,550 shares valued at 45.0 million), with seller debt of 12.3 million assumed in addition, on a preliminary allocation; it was paid in cash and shares, and no borrowings under the Credit Agreement appear in the six months to August 1, 2026 (10-Q Q1 FY27 page:26; 10-Q Q2 FY27 page:4, page:10, page:23, page:35). Management characterizes it as about 175 million of annual revenue run-rate with mid-to-high-teens Adjusted EBITDA margins (Q1 deck page:5); that is Management Language and an unaudited statement.

No new debt issue occurred after August 1, 2026 in the pack, and nothing dated after the cutoff is used. Subsequent event: on August 26, 2026 the Board authorized a new 150.0 million share repurchase program through February 2028, replacing the remaining 83.9 million of the prior authorization (10-Q Q2 FY27 page:30). Prior history: on April 1, 2021 Dycom issued the 4.50% senior notes due 2029; in FY2025 it made three smaller acquisitions of telecommunications contractors (a cash price of 16.0, 24.5 and 150.7 million, 10-K page:99); and the credit agreement was amended and restated in prior years, the latest earlier version dated May 15, 2024 (10-K page:139). The executed Credit Agreement, First Amendment, indenture and both purchase agreements are not in the pack; the terms above are filing summaries (Documentary Fact as described by the issuer, not verified against the executed text).

fields.value: The financial base is usable for the credit snapshot with stated restrictions. All headline figures come from filed statements or from management reconciliations that agree with the filed statements where both exist (the deck-versus-filing items logged by CP-0 do not touch the figures used here). Debt grew from 950.0 million at FY2025 to 2,840.0 million at FY2026 because the Power Solutions acquisition (agreed November 18, 2025, closed December 23, 2025) was financed with a larger Term Loan A and a new Term Loan B (10-K page:112; 10-Q Q2 FY27 page:27, page:48). The Adjusted EBITDA base rose from 576.3 million in FY2025 to 737.7 million in FY2026 and, by construction, to 959.8 million for the last twelve months to August 1, 2026, so reported leverage fell from 3.85x gross at FY2026, the highest of the three periods shown, to 2.96x gross and from 2.89x to 2.61x net. The fall is real in the reported figures, but two effects pull in opposite directions: Building Systems EBITDA enters the base only from December 23, 2025 (and National Technology Integrators from July 2, 2026) while all acquisition debt is already in the numerator, which overstates leverage relative to a pro forma base; and the 53-week FY2026 and LTM spans each include one extra week, which slightly raises the earnings base. Because pre-acquisition EBITDA of the acquired businesses is not supplied, no pro forma ratio can be computed, and the constructed ratios are not covenant ratios.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Interest cover needs the most care. Cash paid for interest was low in FY2026 and in the last twelve months relative to the debt now outstanding, because the Term Loan A increase closed on December 23, 2025 and Term Loan B closed on January 27, 2026, so the added debt carried interest for only part of those periods. A run-rate view built from the Aug 1, 2026 weighted rate of 5.40% on 2,340.0 million of floating-rate term loans plus 22.5 million of fixed note interest gives about 148.9 million a year before fees, and the Q2 2027 interest expense, net annualized gives about 151.9 million; EBITDA cover on those is about 6.45x and 6.32x against 11.10x on reported cash interest. Liquidity at August 1, 2026 is 340.1 million of cash plus 746.4 million of printed revolver availability, with no revolver draw and 53.6 million of standby letters of credit; cash fell from 709.2 million at FY2026 as 238.3 million went to acquisitions and working capital absorbed cash, with accounts receivable, net rising by 520.8 million (520.783 million in the cash flow statement) in the six months to August 1, 2026 that management attributes to growth including acquired balances (10-Q Q2 FY27 page:4, page:49). Free cash flow for those six months was negative 54.2 million against 485.3 million for the last twelve months. Debt maturities are back-ended: nothing falls due before April 2029 apart from small term loan amortization and finance leases, but the composition of the 28.4 million current portion of debt at August 1, 2026 is not printed.

Reporting currency per the context: USD. The context names no sponsor, parent, borrower or guarantor list and supplies no ratings, quotes or deal terms; those are treated as not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Task: build the business and transaction fact pack a committee reads first: which transaction, business, ownership and operating facts matter most to the creditor. Required decision drivers: transaction and ownership structure; business and operating model; credit-relevant history or change. Each fact row carries one of four categories: Documentary Fact (the cited source states it), Management Language (management's characterization, attributed, never adopted), Analyst Interpretation (my reading of cited evidence) and Insufficient Information (evidence missing, with the missing datapoint and why it matters). No information outside the pinned sources is used. Where this handoff gives a financial figure it is the figure in the CP-1 financial base, and a figure that is only in a source is cited to the source. No peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion is made. Periods follow Dycom's fiscal labels: FY2026 is the 53 weeks ended January 31, 2026 and Q2 2027 is the quarter ended August 1, 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business view is clear and well documented; the ownership and governance view is thin. Dycom is a publicly listed contractor, and the pack contains no ownership table or proxy, so control rights, major holders and economic interests are Insufficient Information rather than adverse. What the filings do show is a business whose cash flows come from multi-year master service agreements with a small set of telecom carriers (AT&T, Verizon including Frontier, Lumen), for which customers specify tasks and prices, are generally not committed to volumes and can terminate for convenience (10-K page:9). Evidence to mechanism to implication: the master-service model gives recurring, maintenance-heavy revenue (94.0% of Q2 2027 revenue came from multi-year master service agreements and other long-term contracts, 10-Q Q2 FY27 page:34), which supports revenue durability, but the lack of volume commitments and the concentration mean that a change in one carrier's capital budget, or the AT&T acquisition of Lumen's mass-markets fiber business that closed on February 2, 2026, moves Dycom's revenue and working capital directly. Seasonality, receivable build and unbilled work (1,334,390 thousand of unbilled receivables out of 2,281,043 thousand of gross receivables at August 1, 2026, 10-Q Q2 FY27 page:12) mean cash conversion lags growth, which links to the liquidity and supplier-finance points in the CP-1 financial base.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The transaction view is that FY2026 and FY2027 history is dominated by two acquisitions in a new segment. Power Solutions (agreed November 18, 2025, closed December 23, 2025) was priced at 1.95 billion on a cash-free, debt-free basis and was funded by roughly 85% cash and 15% Dycom shares at signing, with the cash raised through an enlarged Term Loan A, a short-term bridge facility and then a Term Loan B that refinanced the bridge on January 27, 2026 (10-Q Q3 FY26 page:25; 10-K page:99, page:112). National Technology Integrators (agreed May 22, 2026, closed July 2, 2026) added a low-voltage engineering business for a stated price of 275.0 million (10-Q Q1 FY27 page:26; 10-Q Q2 FY27 page:35). The mechanism is that debt-funded growth in a segment with fixed-price and modified fixed-price contracts changes the risk profile from carrier-capex cycle toward project execution, and brings preliminary purchase accounting (goodwill and intangibles now exceed total equity per the CP-1 financial base). The creditor implication is that the earnings base that supports the new leverage was assembled in under a year, is only partly in the trailing figures, and is not yet verified by a full year of combined results. Governance behaviour on the documented evidence is Neutral or Mixed: acquisitions were partly paid in stock, no dividends are paid and no related-party or priming action appears in the pack, but buybacks continued after the leveraging event and a new authorization followed on August 26, 2026. Legal capacity to make distributions cannot be assessed because the credit agreement and indenture are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Power Solutions, LLC (Maryland, electrical infrastructure for data centers and other critical facilities, Greater Washington D.C., Maryland and Virginia area) was acquired under a Unit Purchase Agreement dated November 18, 2025 with Project Eastern Shore, LLC as seller. The preliminary purchase price was 1.95 billion on a cash-free, debt-free basis, payable as a mix of Dycom common stock (1,011,069 shares, 15% of the preliminary price, 292.5 million at signing) and cash, with a purchase price adjustment escrow, a termination right and an outside date of May 18, 2026 (10-Q Q3 FY26 page:25). The deal closed on December 23, 2025: cash of 1,644.9 million (1,628.6 million net of cash acquired), shares valued at 351.0 million at closing and assumed seller debt of 64.8 million, with total consideration of 1,995.9 million in the 10-K (the cash and share amounts together) and 2,008.7 million in the latest 10-Q after a 12.8 million working capital adjustment recorded in Q1 2027; the assumed seller debt is listed separately from total consideration (10-K page:99; 10-Q Q2 FY27 page:35). Status: completed, with the allocation of the purchase price still preliminary in the 10-Q.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financing: on signing, Dycom obtained a debt commitment letter from Bank of America, N.A., BofA Securities, Inc. and Goldman Sachs Bank USA for a 1,000 million senior secured Term Loan A, a 700 million 364-day bridge facility and a 445 million Term Loan A backstop to refinance existing debt (10-Q Q3 FY26 page:25). The executed structure on December 23, 2025 differed: a 600.0 million 364-day secured bridge, Term Loan A increased from 440.0 million to 1,540.0 million, revolver commitments increased from 650.0 million to 800.0 million and maturities extended to December 23, 2030. On January 27, 2026 a First Amendment established an 800 million senior secured Term Loan B, due January 27, 2033, whose proceeds refinanced the bridge, paid fees and funded cash to the balance sheet (10-K page:112). The 4.50% senior notes due 2029 (500.0 million) were not touched. Effect on liquidity and leverage is in the CP-1 financial base: debt of 2,840.0 million at January 31, 2026 against 950.0 million a year earlier, cash of 709.2 million at January 31, 2026, and revolver availability of 746.4 million. Debt issuance costs of 33,870 thousand were paid and a loss on debt extinguishment of 7,268 thousand was recorded in FY2026 (10-K page:83, page:85).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 1. Revenue durability. Evidence: 94.0% of Q2 2027 revenue from multi-year master service agreements and other long-term contracts, with backlog of 12,242 million (10-Q Q2 FY27 page:34, page:55); counter-evidence: customers are not committed to volumes and can terminate for convenience (10-K page:9, page:11). Mechanic: recurring maintenance and program work supports base revenue, but optional volumes make realized revenue track customer capital budgets. Implication: revenue is more durable than a project contractor's but not contractually floored; backlog is an indicator, not a commitment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 2. Concentration. Evidence: AT&T, Verizon and Lumen at 25.4%, 14.0% and 10.8% of FY2026 revenue (10-K page:9), and a receivable-plus-contract-asset concentration in four customers (10-Q Q2 FY27 page:13). Mechanic: customer mergers (Verizon with Frontier, AT&T with Lumen's fiber business) reshuffle the customer set and change who controls build budgets and payment timing. Implication: cash collection and revenue timing depend on a few counterparties; a delay by one carrier shows up in days sales outstanding and liquidity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 3. Margin and cash-flow risk. Evidence: Communications margins are seasonal and depend on operating leverage (10-K page:10; 10-Q Q2 FY27 page:46); Building Systems margin is higher in the latest quarter (CP-1 segments) but is on fixed-price work with preliminary accounting (10-K page:11; 10-Q Q2 FY27 page:10). Mechanic: fixed-price contracts transfer cost overruns to Dycom, and receivable growth absorbs cash. Implication: margin and free cash flow can diverge from Adjusted EBITDA, which the CP-1 base shows through the six-month free cash flow figure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 4. Transaction leverage. Evidence: debt of 2,840.0 million at January 31, 2026 against 950.0 million a year earlier (CP-1). Mechanic: acquisition debt came before a full year of acquired earnings. Implication: constructed leverage is sensitive to pro forma earnings that are not supplied, and to buybacks that compete with repayment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 5. Sponsor alignment. Evidence: public company, no sponsor in the context, ownership not in the pack. Mechanic: no controlling-holder incentives can be identified or excluded. Implication: neutral on sponsor risk with an explicit information gap.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 6. Key uncertainties: the executed documents, restricted-payment capacity, pro forma EBITDA, supplier finance terms and the covenant ratios. Counter-evidence logged above does not alter these; it concerns purchase accounting values.

fields.value: Task: synthesize the fundamental credit view a committee reads first, from the settled upstream handoffs only: the CP-1 financial base and the CP-1A business and transaction registers, with CP-0 for source limits. Required decision drivers are business risk (from the business and transaction handoff), financial risk and liquidity (from the financial base figures), and the gaps that limit both. This handoff opens no source text and quotes nothing: every row rests on a figure or row in an upstream handoff, and a figure appears here exactly as it appears there. Each conclusion carries one of four categories: Documentary Fact (an upstream handoff states it from a filing), Management Language (management's characterization carried upstream, qualified, never adopted), Analyst Interpretation (my reading of the upstream basis) or Insufficient Information (the basis is missing, with the missing datapoint stated). Missing evidence is never read as an adverse conclusion. No peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion is made. Periods: FY2025 is the 52 weeks ended January 25, 2025; FY2026 is the 53 weeks ended January 31, 2026; Q2 2027 is the quarter ended August 1, 2026; LTM Q2 2027 is the constructed 53-week last-twelve-months period to August 1, 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: These seven sources are the evidence base of the upstream handoffs. This module did not reopen them; it relies on them only through the handoffs below, which cite their locators.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fundamental credit view is that Dycom is a scaled, cash-generative specialty contractor with solid liquidity, whose financial risk was raised sharply by a debt-funded step into data-center electrical work and which carries meaningful customer concentration; the view is held with Medium confidence (Analyst Interpretation). It rests on three links from evidence to mechanism to implication.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: First, business risk. Evidence: 94.0% of Q2 2027 revenue came from multi-year master service agreements and other long-term contracts, backlog was 12,242 million at August 1, 2026 with 6,472 million expected in the next twelve months, but customers are generally not committed to specific volumes and can terminate for convenience, and AT&T, Verizon and Lumen supplied 25.4%, 14.0% and 10.8% of FY2026 revenue (Documentary Fact, business and transaction handoff and financial base). Mechanism: recurring maintenance and program work gives revenue durability, while the absence of volume commitments and the concentration make realized revenue track a few carriers' capital budgets, and customer mergers (Verizon with Frontier, AT&T with Lumen's fiber business) reshuffle those budgets. Implication: revenue visibility is better than for a project contractor but is not a contractual floor, so default risk through the cycle depends on the carriers' continued build programs and on working capital discipline.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Second, financial risk. Evidence: notional debt rose from 950.0 million at FY2025 to 2,840.0 million at FY2026 and 2,842.7 million at August 1, 2026; constructed leverage was 3.85x gross and 2.89x net at FY2026 and 2.96x gross and 2.61x net on LTM Q2 2027 Adjusted EBITDA of 959.8 million, against 1.65x gross and 1.49x net at FY2025 (Documentary Fact inputs, constructed ratios; financial base). Mechanism: the acquisition debt arrived before a full year of acquired earnings, so the constructed ratios are not pro forma and are not covenant ratios, and about 82% of debt was floating-rate with no interest-rate hedge disclosed. Cash interest cover of 11.10x on LTM cash interest of 86.4 million is overstated by the timing of the new debt; the run-rate view of about 148.9 million of interest gives about 6.45x and the Q2 2027 annualized interest view of about 151.9 million gives about 6.32x. Implication: leverage tolerance is adequate on reported figures, debt service remains adequately covered even on run-rate interest, but the cushion is thinner than the headline cash cover suggests and is exposed to Term SOFR, with a 50 basis point move changing annual interest by about 11.7 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Third, liquidity and refinancing. Evidence: cash of 340.1 million plus 746.4 million of undrawn revolver gives liquidity of 1,086.5 million at August 1, 2026, with 53.6 million of standby letters of credit and no revolver draw; the only scheduled amortization visible is 4.0 million in FY2027 and the first large maturity is the 500.0 million 4.50% notes due April 2029, then Term Loan A and the revolver in December 2030 and Term Loan B in January 2033 (financial base). Mechanism: back-ended maturities with a large undrawn revolver limit near-term refinancing pressure. Counter-evidence: cash fell from 709.2 million at FY2026 to 340.1 million at August 1, 2026, free cash flow for the six months was negative 54.2 million after a 520.8 million receivables build, supplier finance of 367.4 million sits inside accounts payable, and the revolver availability computation and the composition of the 28.4 million current portion of debt are not printed. Implication: liquidity is the strongest mitigant, but it is working-capital sensitive and not backed by visible covenant headroom.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would weaken if combined-business earnings run materially below the LTM base, if a major carrier cuts or defers programs (management already deferred about 150 million of Communications wireless revenue into fiscal 2028, Management Language), or if buybacks outpace deleveraging. It would strengthen if full-year pro forma EBITDA confirms leverage near the constructed range and covenant compliance computations show wide headroom. Neither can be confirmed from the pack.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: First, the leverage story is a step-up and a partial reversal. Debt of 2,840.0 million at FY2026 against 950.0 million a year earlier reflects the Power Solutions acquisition, and constructed gross leverage of 2.96x at August 1, 2026 is below the 3.85x at FY2026 only because the LTM earnings base now includes Building Systems and strong Communications growth; the ratios are not pro forma, not covenant ratios and sensitive to the 53-week FY2026 (Documentary Fact inputs, Analyst Interpretation). Second, interest burden is understated by cash interest: LTM cash interest of 86.4 million sits well below the run-rate of about 148.9 million, so the reported cover of 11.10x is a ceiling and about 6.45x the cautious figure. Third, liquidity is large but not unconditional: 1,086.5 million of liquidity, no revolver draw and a maturity wall that starts in April 2029, offset by cash that fell from 709.2 million at FY2026 to 340.1 million at August 1, 2026, a negative six-month free cash flow of 54.2 million and 367.4 million of supplier finance. Fourth, customer concentration and uncommitted volumes make revenue sensitive to a few carriers, with backlog of 12,242 million an indicator rather than a commitment. Fifth, Building Systems is both the growth driver and the newest risk: Q2 2027 revenue of 397.5 million and Non-GAAP Adjusted EBITDA of 97.2 million on fixed-price and modified-fixed-price work, with a preliminary purchase price allocation for National Technology Integrators and goodwill plus intangibles of 2,534.3 million exceeding equity of 2,063.9 million. Sixth, the information that would settle the credit view is missing: the executed credit agreement and indenture, covenant EBITDA and ratios, pro forma acquired EBITDA, ownership and restricted-payment capacity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. Recurring contract base and backlog: 94.0% of Q2 2027 revenue from multi-year master service agreements and other long-term contracts and backlog of 12,242 million support revenue durability (Documentary Fact). Liquidity and maturity profile: 1,086.5 million of liquidity, 746.4 million of undrawn revolver, and a first major maturity in April 2029 limit refinancing risk (Documentary Fact inputs). Earnings and cash generation: Adjusted EBITDA of 737.7 million in FY2026 against 576.3 million in FY2025 and 959.8 million on LTM Q2 2027, with LTM free cash flow of 485.3 million (Documentary Fact inputs, constructed LTM). Equity used in acquisitions and no dividends: part of the Power Solutions and National Technology Integrators consideration was paid in shares and no cash dividend is paid, which limits cash leakage (Documentary Fact; the behavior reading of Neutral or Mixed is Analyst Interpretation). Higher-margin diversification: Building Systems Adjusted EBITDA of 97.2 million on revenue of 397.5 million in Q2 2027 broadens the earnings base beyond carrier fiber work (Documentary Fact for the figures; durability of the margin is Analyst Interpretation because the contracts are fixed-price and the allocation is preliminary).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. Customer concentration: AT&T, Verizon and Lumen supplied 50.2% of FY2026 revenue combined by customer name, customers may terminate for convenience and are not committed to volumes (Documentary Fact). Leverage step-up and floating-rate exposure: debt of 2,842.7 million at August 1, 2026, about 82% floating-rate at FY2026, no interest-rate hedge disclosed (Documentary Fact; constructed ratios are Analyst Interpretation). Interest cover cushion thinner than headline: about 6.45x on run-rate interest against 11.10x on cash interest (Analyst Interpretation on constructed inputs). Working capital intensity: days sales outstanding of 101, unbilled receivables of 1,334,390 thousand of 2,281,043 thousand gross receivables, and a negative six-month free cash flow of 54.2 million (Documentary Fact). Claims outside the debt figure: supplier finance of 367.4 million, performance and other surety bonds of 1,215.8 million and operating lease liabilities of 228.7 million (Documentary Fact; sensitivity to supplier finance withdrawal is Analyst Interpretation). Asset base is largely intangible: goodwill plus intangible assets of 2,534.3 million exceed total stockholders' equity of 2,063.9 million, so tangible net worth is negative, which is a mechanic for loss absorption rather than a recovery conclusion (Documentary Fact inputs, constructed comparison). Financial policy opacity: new 150.0 million buyback authorization on August 26, 2026 beside rising debt, with restricted-payment capacity, covenant EBITDA and ownership information unavailable (Documentary Fact and Insufficient Information).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No risk is rated Critical: nothing in the upstream registers indicates a near-term liquidity shortfall, a covenant breach (compliance is stated, though not shown) or a maturity within the next twelve months beyond small amortization.

The ratios and the LTM aggregates are constructed in the financial base, where their inputs and formulas are shown: LTM Adjusted EBITDA of 959.8 million (FY2026 737.7 less 355.9 plus 578.0, cross-checked against four discrete quarters), total debt over Adjusted EBITDA of 2.96x (2,842.7 over 959.8), net debt over Adjusted EBITDA of 2.61x (2,502.6 over 959.8), cash interest cover of 11.10x (959.8 over 86.4) and run-rate interest cover of about 6.45x (959.8 over about 148.9). fields.value: Task: validate the evidence trace behind every material claim in the run, and the integrity of the story the modules tell together. Evaluated set: the source readiness handoff (CP-0), the financial base (CP-1), the business and transaction registers (CP-1A) and the fundamental credit synthesis (CP-2). Scope is the default Top 5 material credit drivers, with a statement-level lineage register for the claims that carry them. This is a governance layer: it does not change upstream conclusions, adds no new credit analysis, and does not silently repair a defect; where it finds one it logs it with the fix the owner should make. Because accepted handoffs cannot be edited, every correction is stated here. I re-opened the pinned sources for 53 located checks (a located quote on the cited page for each figure or fact tested), recomputed the derived figures independently, and compared figures across the four handoffs. Periods follow Dycom's fiscal labels: FY2025 is the 52 weeks ended January 25, 2025; FY2026 is the 53 weeks ended January 31, 2026; Q2 2027 is the quarter ended August 1, 2026; LTM Q2 2027 is the constructed 53-week last-twelve-months period to August 1, 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, evidence traceability is Ready with Remediation. Of the Top 5 material credit drivers, 2 are directly sourced, 1 is calculated, 1 is assumption-based, 1 is an analyst inference, and 0 are weak-lineage, untraced, conflicting, or insufficient-information items. The most important provenance gap is the absence of the executed Credit Agreement, its First Amendment and the notes indenture together with pro forma EBITDA for the acquired businesses, which matters because every leverage, cover and headroom conclusion then traces to Dycom's management EBITDA and a non-pro-forma last-twelve-months base rather than to the lenders' covenant definitions, and it implies that committee use of leverage-based conclusions is Restricted until those inputs are obtained.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Method of the trace: for each Top 5 driver I read the claim in the handoff that makes it, opened the pinned source at the cited page and confirmed the quoted figure, then followed every derived figure back to its inputs and recomputed it. The 53 located checks cover customer concentration, contract mix, backlog, cash, revolver availability, supplier finance, liquidity, the weighted interest rate, the floating-rate share, the interest-rate sensitivity, Adjusted EBITDA for each discrete quarter and period, cash interest, debt carrying values, the extra-week revenue amounts, the Power Solutions consideration and share value, unbilled receivables, days sales outstanding, contractual obligations, the current portion of debt, buyback authorizations, employees, shares outstanding, the date of the National Technology Integrators transaction and the ownership statement. All 53 matched. The defects below are therefore about wording, basis and completeness, not about transcription of sourced figures. The strongest contrary evidence to a clean trace is that most ratios are constructed by the analyst chain rather than printed by the issuer, and the set contains two management-versus-filing or filing-versus-filing differences that no source resolves. What would make that evidence win: if the executed credit documents show a covenant EBITDA materially different from management Adjusted EBITDA, every ratio in this set would need restating on that basis.
